/-!
# Conjecture 4.65

by J. G. Thompson

Conjecture: $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

The notebook remarks that the validity of this conjecture would simplify the proof of
solvability of groups of odd order (W. Feit, J. G. Thompson, *Pacific J. Math.* **13**, no. 3
(1963), 775–1029), rendering unnecessary the detailed use of generators and relations.

This is the Feit–Thompson conjecture on primes; see also
`FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture`, which states it for $p < q$ only.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.65
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

blocks.docstring:
Conjecture: $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

Both quotients are positive natural numbers, since $p - 1 \mid p^q - 1$ and
$q - 1 \mid q^p - 1$, so natural-number division here is exact.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop over all distinct primes p, q (both orderings, so equivalent to the p<q form in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture.lean, which states the same open conjecture); natural-number division is exact here since p-1 ∣ p^q-1, and the subsequent sentence about simplifying the Feit–Thompson odd-order proof is motivation, not a question (the stronger gcd=1 version is false, Stephens 1971, but is not what the statement asks).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical proposition: ∀ p q : ℕ, p.Prime → q.Prime → p ≠ q → ¬ (p^q-1)/(p-1) ∣ (q^p-1)/(q-1). This matches the source verbatim: distinct primes (both orderings via p ≠ q), literal divisibility direction, and ℕ division which I verified in Lean is exact (Nat.sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow gives p-1 ∣ p^q-1) with both quotients positive for primes (via Nat.geomSum_eq), so no 0-divisibility or truncation artifacts. Parsing of ¬ over the whole ∣ also verified by rfl. c07 chosen for its hypotheses-as-arguments style (matching FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture.lean) and complete docstrings citing the notebook remark and the Wikipedia cross-reference; c02/c03/c06 are equivalent alternatives, and c01/c04/c05/c08 differ only in binder style or sparser docstrings.

/-!
# Conjecture 4.65

by J. G. Thompson

Conjecture: $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

The notebook remarks that the validity of this conjecture would simplify the proof of
solvability of groups of odd order (W. Feit, J. G. Thompson, *Pacific J. Math.* **13**, no. 3
(1963), 775–1029), rendering unnecessary the detailed use of generators and relations.

This is the Feit–Thompson conjecture on primes; see also
`FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture`, which states it for $p < q$ only.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.65
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.65»

/--
Conjecture: $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

Both quotients are positive natural numbers, since $p - 1 \mid p^q - 1$ and
$q - 1 \mid q^p - 1$, so natural-number division here is exact.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.65» (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ¬ (p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1) ∣ (q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.65»

items: The item is a conjecture (an assertion), not a question, so the repository's plain `theorem : P` style is used rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ …`.

Used ℕ with truncated subtraction and floor division, literally mirroring the source's (p^q-1)/(p-1). This is exact for primes (p ≥ 2 and p-1 ∣ p^q-1); an alternative would have been the geometric sum ∑ i < q, p^i, which is equal but less literal.

Quantified over all distinct primes with hypotheses `p ≠ q` as theorem arguments (both orderings), matching the source; this is equivalent to the `p < q` form in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture.lean (which has the roles of p and q swapped), since the conjecture is quantified symmetrically.
Divisibility direction kept literal: (p^q-1)/(p-1) is the divisor, (q^p-1)/(q-1) the dividend.
AMS tags 11 (number theory, the statement itself) and 20 (group theory, the notebook's motivation via the odd-order theorem).

The remark about simplifying the Feit–Thompson odd-order proof is recorded in the module docstring as motivation only and is not formalized; the false gcd = 1 strengthening (Stephens 1971) is not stated, as it is not what the notebook asks.

reviewer_notes: The statement is a declarative conjecture, not a question, so no answer(sorry) is used. The sentence about simplifying the Feit–Thompson odd-order proof is motivation only and is recorded in the docstring, not formalized. Uses AMS 11 20 (number theory content; group-theoretic motivation in a group-theory collection) — a reviewer may prefer AMS 11 alone; this is not a faithfulness issue. The final file is the existing Wikipedia formalization's twin with p ≠ q instead of p < q (both orderings), exactly as the notebook says. Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
